card.italy_title: {n} M6+ earthquakes in the Apennines since {year}

earthquake-prediction.image: the app's magnitude widget at M6.0, with circles for M4.0, M5.0 and M6.0 whose areas show the energy released (each step about 32 times more), an estimated energy of about 15 kilotons of TNT and about 158 such earthquakes a year worldwide

plate-tectonics-subduction.image: a cross-section of a convergent plate boundary: an oceanic plate bends down beneath a continental plate, with a volcano on the continent above the sinking slab

faults-and-stress.image: a cross-section of a normal fault: layered rock cut by a dashed fault line, arrows pulling the two sides apart and the hanging wall sliding down past the footwall

earth-interior-seismic-waves.image: a grid of particles showing a P wave: the rock compresses and stretches along the direction of travel, with one column of particles highlighted

aftershocks-and-hazards.image: two charts: recent earthquakes grouped by depth (shallow, intermediate and deep, most of them shallow) and the number of aftershocks per day after a mainshock, falling quickly over ten days as Omori's law describes

surface-waves-and-damage.image: the app's seismic wave widget on the Surface tab: a grid of particles moving in a rolling wave along the direction of travel

magnitude-scales.image: the app's magnitude widget at M6.0, with circles for M4.0, M5.0 and M6.0 whose areas show the energy released (each step about 32 times more), an estimated energy of about 15 kilotons of TNT and about 158 such earthquakes a year worldwide

deep-focus-earthquakes.image: a cross-section of a convergent plate boundary: an oceanic plate sinks beneath a continental plate, with earthquakes tracing the slab down to about 700 km

volcano-seismology.image: a world map of recent M4.5+ earthquakes, with those on the Ring of Fire, the belt of ocean trenches and volcanoes around the Pacific, highlighted

italian-earthquakes.image: an outline of Italy with the M6+ earthquakes of the Apennines since 1279 from the INGV CPTI15 catalogue, sized by magnitude, with Norcia 2016, L'Aquila 2009, Irpinia 1980 and Marsica 1915 labelled
